prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1162; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received by phone from the claimant, who reports a low-speed head-on collision at a residential intersection earlier today. The claimant states they were the driver of the insured vehicle and complains of neck pain.

Entry 2: Recorded a detailed statement from the claimant, who described the sequence of events and the approach of the other vehicle in the same way as in the first call. Confirmed the claimant was seated in the driver's seat at the time of impact.

Entry 3: Spoke with the other driver, who independently confirmed the vehicles collided head-on at low speed and that the claimant was behind the wheel. Their account matches the claimant's description of the collision.

Entry 4: Reviewed the police report, which lists the claimant as a vehicle occupant and records the same location, time of impact, and direction of travel. Report notes no citations were issued.

Entry 5: Obtained scene photographs and two witness statements. Both witnesses describe a minor impact consistent with what the claimant and the other driver reported.

Entry 6: Inspected the insured vehicle. Front-end damage is consistent with the reported impact. A few old scratches on the lower bumper may predate this loss and have been noted separately for the repair estimate.

Entry 7: Confirmed with the policy records that coverage was in force on the date of loss and that no prior claims or damage reports exist for this vehicle. Nothing in the file suggests damage occurred before coverage began.

Entry 8: Verified that the claimant is a household member of the policyholder and lives at the same address, so they qualify as a covered driver under the policy.

Entry 9: Claimant has reported neck stiffness and headaches to the treating provider. The provider's notes indicate a whiplash-type injury, which is a plausible result of a collision of this kind. No prior treatment to the neck or upper back appears in the records available.

Entry 10: Treatment has followed a typical course of physical therapy and medication. Claimant reports steady improvement, and the frequency of visits has decreased as recovery progressed.

Entry 11: Called the claimant for a status update. Claimant repeated the same account of the accident and the symptoms, with no changes to the timeline or the injuries described earlier.

Entry 12: Reviewed the file as of today. Liability and coverage are confirmed, the injury appears consistent with the collision, and treatment is tapering as expected. Recommended proceeding with the standard evaluation of the bodily injury claim.
